headline: Israeli Strike Kills 2 Workers at Gaza Clinic, Doctors Without Borders Says

paragraphs.text: Doctors Without Borders, the aid group, said an Israeli strike on Friday killed two workers at one of its clinics in Gaza, the latest in a series of deadly attacks in the territory in recent days. Israel has said that the attacks targeted Hamas officials.

“We are devastated and outraged by the killing of two of our colleagues, both watchmen, in an Israeli strike on one of our Gaza clinics tonight,” Doctors Without Borders said in a statement, adding that its facilities were clearly marked as medical buildings. It said the location of the clinic had been shared with the Israeli military and that the deaths brought to 17 the number of Doctors Without Borders workers killed in Gaza.

The Israeli military said in a statement that the men were “Hamas terrorists working under humanitarian cover” as security guards who were preparing attacks against Israeli civilians and troops, without providing any evidence for its claims. The military added that it had taken “precautionary measures” to minimize harm to civilians and that “no damage was caused to medical infrastructure.”
Doctors Without Borders did not immediately respond to a request for comment about the Israeli military’s assertions about the workers.

The strike came at the end of a week of intensifying and deadly attacks on Gaza that have killed at least three Hamas officials, according to the Israeli military, despite a nominal U.S.-backed cease-fire that took effect in October 2025. At least 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the truce was reached, according to Gaza’s health ministry, which does not distinguish between civilians and combatants.

On Thursday, an Israeli strike killed Khaled Abu Nada, a Hamas official and Gaza’s deputy minister of education, along with his wife, according to the authorities in Gaza. Israel accused him of directing funds toward Hamas’s armed forces.

Following the killing of Mr. Abu Nada, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel said in a statement that the Israeli military had killed roughly 80 members of Hamas during the past month and vowed to continue pursuing the group’s leaders and operatives.
Hamas said the “assassination” of its leaders violated the cease-fire.

Israel has escalated strikes as Mr. Netanyahu fights for his political life following an inconclusive Israeli election last month. The prime minister is serving as a caretaker leader, with Israeli opposition parties in negotiations to form a new government.

Mr. Netanyahu has been dogged by public anger over the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, attack in which roughly 1,200 people were killed. The prime minister has regularly raised the specter of further violence targeting Israelis as he bids to remain in power.

In January, Doctors Without Borders said Israel had ordered it to cease operations in Gaza. The Israeli authorities said the aid organization had failed to comply with restrictions that include registering all Gazan employees so that they could be vetted and limiting its criticism of Israel’s conduct of the war. More than 74,000 Palestinians have been killed in Israel’s war in Gaza in response to the Oct. 7 attack, according to local health officials, and much of the territory has been reduced to rubble.

Doctors Without Borders and other aid groups said the demands contravened international law and violated workers’ privacy rights and European data-protection rules that such groups were legally obligated to follow.
